title: fix(components): a rail card and a tab badge over the same list share one read (objectui#13010 part 4)
body:
Part of #13010
Clause-②: yes (widening: three additive members on the exported `RelatedCountStore`; amended by the PM seat)

Part 4 of objectui#13010: Wanted item 1's remainder. A record page that shows the same unfiltered related list as a `record:reference_rail` card and in a `page:tabs` count badge now reads it once on open, not twice. Item 1's other halves (part 1, PR #13019) and parts 2 and 3 are outside this PR, so the card stays open.

## What changed

The design is candidate X from the order. I measured it and it holds without relying on timing.

- `RelatedCountStore` (`packages/components/src/hooks/related-count-store.ts`):
  - The rail claims rows with `claimRows(object, relationshipField, parentId, rowCap)`. When the badge probe (`fetch`) finds a claim on its unfiltered key, it sends `$top: rowCap` with `$count: true` instead of `$top: 1`. The store holds those rows until the rail takes them.
  - `fetchRows` is the rail's read. It takes held rows, or joins an in-flight read that asked for enough rows. Otherwise it sends its own read and registers it as in flight, so a badge probe that comes later joins it for the total.
  - Both sides send the same query through one helper (`startRead`): same `composeParentScopeFilter`, same `total` read.
- `record:reference_rail` (`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-reference-rail.tsx`):
  - The rail claims its entries **while rendering**. Every render in a commit finishes before any effect in it runs, so the claim is made before the tab strip's probe effect, with no reliance on effect, microtask or frame order.
  - The first read of a scope goes through `fetchRows`. The wire is unchanged: `$filter`, `$top: rowCap`, `$count: true`.
  - A refresh (a bus invalidation) still reads directly, never from the store.
  - An effect claims again after a StrictMode remount, and releases the claim on unmount or when the scope changes.
- `containers.tsx` is **not** changed. The probe effect still calls `RelatedCountStore.fetch` as before, and the store decides `$top`.
- No new module export. The three new members sit on the existing `RelatedCountStore` object, which is the only path the rail has to the store.

## Rulings held

- **Never a count from another filter.** A badge with a declared filter has a different store key, so it never sees the card's claim and keeps its own `$top: 1` probe. Rail entries declare no filter, so claims exist only on unfiltered keys.
- **No cache beyond this record open.** Held rows are a hand-off: the rail takes them once. An invalidation of the child object drops them, and so does the rail's unmount (or a change of scope). An invalidation also drops reads that went out before the change, so nothing asked after the change joins a read from before it.
- **The visibility gate stays.** A claim reads nothing on its own, so a rail alone on the page reads only once it is visible.
- **No stale rows after a refresh (objectui#12244).** A refresh re-reads directly.

## Where the claim cannot come first

If the badge's probe is sent before the rail has rendered at all (the rail is in a region that renders in a later commit), the probe asks for one row. The rail cannot use that read, so it reads for itself. That is two reads, as before this PR, and the answer is still correct. On the harness page (HotCRM-shaped) the rail and the strip render in one commit, so this case does not arise there.

## Wave table: the part-1 harness (`RecordDetailView.recordOpenWaves-13010.test.tsx`)

Before, at `4016370af3`: 13 requests, all in wave 1. Quote and line are each read twice.

```
w1 GET /api/v1/approvals/requests
w1 POST /api/v1/security/explain {update}

w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_deal/rec-13010
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_user top=50
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_comment
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_activity top=200
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_quote top=1
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_line top=1
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_task top=1
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_quote top=3
```

After, at `b94d1a2272`: 11 requests, all in wave 1. Quote and line are each read once with `top=3`. The task badge (its own declared filter) and the task card remain two different questions.

```

w1 POST /api/v1/security/explain {update}
w1 POST /api/v1/security/explain {delete}
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_deal/rec-13010
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_user top=50
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_comment
w1 GET /api/v1/data/sys_activity top=200
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_quote top=3
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_line top=3
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_task top=1
w1 GET /api/v1/data/os_13010_task top=3
```

## Pins

- **(a)** Harness: `each unfiltered relation the rail and the tab badge both show is ONE read, and both are drawn`. Quote and line each have exactly one read (`top=3`). The Related tab badge draws 17 (6 + 7 + the filtered task probe's 4). Each card draws rows 0 to 2 (no row 3) and its own total.
- **(b) controls:**
  - Harness: `CONTROL: a badge whose declared filter differs from its card still probes, with its own filter`, and the part-1 wave-1 pin. Both still pass.
  - `record-reference-rail.sharedRead-13010.test.tsx` covers:
    - both orders: badge first, read settled, rail visible later; badge first with the rail visible while the read is out; rail first
    - a rail alone waits for visibility (no read)
    - a rail alone reads its own rows once visible, on the old wire
    - a filtered badge keeps its one-row probe
    - a refresh reads again and draws the new rows although the store had held rows
    - the rail's unmount releases its claim
  - `related-count-store.sharedRead-13010.test.ts`: with no claim, the probe is byte-identical to before. Also pinned: rows are taken once; a claim never reaches a filtered probe; an invalidation drops held rows; an invalidation while the probe is out leaves nothing to hand over and nothing to join; a release drops held rows; a failed shared read rejects for the card and reads 0 for the badge.
- **Ablation** (run once, through objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): the mutation replaced `const claimed = filter === undefined ? claims.get(k) : undefined;` with `const claimed = undefined;`, which drops the sharing. Anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the blob from `872f791187f8` to `dacf43eb883a`. The harness ran with 1 failure and 3 passes. Pin (a) failed with `expected [ 1, 3 ] to deeply equal [ 3 ]` for `os_13010_quote`, and the other three stayed green. The restore was proven by blob `872f791187f8` equal to HEAD, with `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Verification (head `b94d1a2272`)

- **vitest** (under the shared lock, `--maxWorkers=1`): 28 files, 177 tests, all passed. The files are the `related-count-store*`, `record-reference-rail*`, `page-tabs*` (incl. `page-tabs-probe-route-id-13010`), `RecordDetailView.related*`, `RecordDetailView.recordOpenWaves-13010` and `RecordDetailView.childWriteRefreshesParent-12244` families, plus the two new files.
- **Closure build:** `--filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...'` exited 0.
- **`type-check`** (`tsc --noEmit` plus `tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0 for `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell`.
- **eslint** `--no-inline-config` on the 5 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 0 errors. Warnings equal the base on both source files: store 3 = 3, rail 11 = 11. The two new test files have 8 `no-explicit-any` warnings.
- **Gate battery, exit 0:** check:phantom-deps, self-import, unreferenced-sources, doc-example-readers, handler-key-reads, side-effects-array, element-data-source-declaration, spec-symbols, action-forward-parity, designer-field-key-parity, icon-record-names, i18n-keys, i18n-drift, i18n-designer-parity, control-bytes, test-path-roots, new-line-citations, vi-mock-specifiers, vi-mock-inherit; check-hand-rolled-comment-mask, check-changeset-fixed, check-changeset-presence, check-changeset-no-major.
- **`check:spec-floors`** exits 1 (`no-artifact`: it needs a whole-workspace build). NOT MEASURED, recorded and not fixed, per the order.
- **Declared to CI:** the full package directories of `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell`, and repo-wide `pnpm lint`.

## Acceptance notes

- A child write still costs two reads for a list that both the rail and the badge show. The badge's re-probe after the invalidation is the claimed `top=N` read, and the rail's refresh reads directly. That is the same count as before this PR. This card is about the record open.
- In development StrictMode, React's simulated unmount releases the claim, and the effect claims again in the same commit. A badge probe that went out between the two without awaiting a schema read would ask for one row and fall back to two reads. Production has no simulated unmount.
- `invalidate` now also drops in-flight reads for the keys it clears. A badge re-probe that comes right after a change sends a fresh read rather than joining one from before the change.
